subject: Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster

messages.author: e728ca3dc3a1a072
messages.subject: Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster
parts:
Hi,

I've been using packages "snow" and "rlecuyer" along with the n.cluster= argument in the scan two function to run my permutations on an HPC cluster and it has worked well.

However, my analyses seem to be timing out, and I'm getting some output I haven't encountered before (see below). I think there has been some update to the "snow" package such that my code no longer works in parallel.

Any thoughts on how to update my code to get things working again?

Many thanks,

Chris




> library(snow)
> library(qtl)
Loading required package: parallel

Attaching package: ‘parallel’

The following object(s) are masked from ‘package:snow’:

    clusterApply, clusterApplyLB, clusterCall, clusterEvalQ,
    clusterExport, clusterMap, clusterSplit, makeCluster, parApply,
    parCapply, parLapply, parRapply, parSapply, splitIndices,
    stopCluster

> library(rlecuyer)

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster
parts:
R/qtl is now using the parallel package in place of snow and rlecuyer.
You shouldn't need to load the snow library anymore.

What particular functions are you using, that no longer seem to be giving a speed-up?
What operating system are you using?

karl

messages.author: e728ca3dc3a1a072
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster
parts:
Karl,

I'm having problems on a cluster running Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6.3 (RHEL6.3), using Torque for resource management, and MOAB for job management. Getting permutations from scantwo is what seems to be bottoming out. I typically break up the job across 8 nodes with 4 cores per node (and use n.cluster=31), which always seems to get me 10K permutations in about 15 minutes. Most of my analyses now are running, but they seem to take 4 hours or more. I'm wondering if there is a problem with parallel being able to split the job across both multiple nodes and multiple cores per node. I've been in communication with our system admin, but he says that everything looks fine and it is difficult to troubleshoot.

On my own machine (OS 10.7), running R 2.15.1 with qtl version 1.25-15, everything works fine. I run the permutations on 6 cores and it takes about an hour. The trouble is that I have a lot of phenotypes to run and I rather not subject my computer to the sustained high temps.

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: e728ca3dc3a1a072
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster
parts:
Karl,

I've done a few tests and it looks to me like parallel is able to split the work across multiple cores on a single compute node, but is not effectively splitting the work across multiple compute nodes. For example, an analysis using 8 cores on one compute node (n.cluster=8) and and an analysis using 8 cores on each of two compute nodes (n.cluster=16) both in practice only use 8 cores and both take an equivalent amount of time.

I think RAM isn't a limiting factor. I've been allocating 3Gb of RAM per core/cluster, and they seem to use about 1.7Gb of that. I've done the same analysis doubling the RAM with no increase in speed.

Is there a possible solution for getting the parallel package to perform in a high performance computing cluster?

Thanks again,

Chris

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster
parts:
Oh, I see.  I have to admit that I didn't pay full attention to what you were saying initially.

Yes, within an instance of R, scantwo permutations won't be split across nodes but will just use the multiple CPUs within a node. I don't know how to split a task across multiple nodes from within R, and from what I'd seen in the distant past, it would be quite system-dependent.

Personally, I'd just creat a bunch of R scripts for separate R CMD BATCH runs, and then use your job scheduler to spawn and manage the jobs.

karl

messages.author: 92292fc48bf46044
messages.subject: Re: Problems with scan two permutations on a cluster
parts:
Dear Chris,

You could use the function makePSOCKcluster, it functions the same way as the makeSOCKcluster from SNOW
You could use this to do permutation on multiple nodes like:

cl <- makePSOCKcluster(c("node1.cluster.uni.edu", "node1.cluster.uni.edu", "node2.cluster.uni.edu"))

You could replace the makeCluster call inside scantwo by a custom cluster call for your cluster
But using the scheduler is probably easier

For information about makePSOCKcluster see the SNOW docs: http://homepage.stat.uiowa.edu/~luke/R/cluster/cluster.html
Under sockets

Gr,
Danny
